newsitem.title: UK: Med and Caribs crude tanker rates slip on supply.
newsitem.headline: Med and Caribs crude tanker rates slip on supply.

text.p: Crude tanker rates were mostly steady on Tuesday, bar the cross Mediterranean market and Caribs sector which were under pressure of plentiful tonnage.
Mideast rates for VLCCs to Singapore were down slightly to just below W57.5, while Mideast/west voyages were unchanged at W52.5.

The West Africa/U.S. Gulf market was also on a level with last week, with VLCCs at W65 and W70 for fixtures to the UK/Cont. Smaller Suezmaxes from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf came down a little to W85.
The cross-Mediterranean chartering theatre was mixed with prompt ships difficult to obtain and rates high, while mid-July loading dates were paralled with a surfeit of tonange.

Forward fixtures around the middle of July were being settled between W115 and W120, but brokers said the market would be extremely tight for loading dates before July 15 and charterers would have to pay higher rates..
"The market hasn't changed, but it's getting very tight to find a ship," said one London broker.
A second broker said even after July 15 a charterer could be looking at rates as high as W120, but for a prompt ship as high as W160 was feasible.
"If you're dates are between 5-10 July you're going to be very stuck," he added. "There's not one ship available."
Caribs/up U.S.coast rates meanwhile were off five points due to good tonnage availability, and brokers said they saw them slipping lower.
"The market has fallen down," said a U.S. broker. "A lot of ships are showing up and there are less cargos. I think we're going to see it hitting even lower."
An Exxon fixture for 77,500 tonnes was set at W140 to the U.S. Gulf, a level seen reflecting the current market.

In the North Sea busy for transatlantic VLCCs and Suezmaxes was very quiet with no vessels seen getting fixed. Shipbrokers said rates were around W65 and W85 respectively. Crude traders said it was unlikely cargoes would be fixed transatlantic given current ight wet supplies in NWE.
For 80,000 tonners plying inter UK/Cont trade rates were put between W115-120 depending on load/discharge ports.
